questions.text: Compare Computer Architecture vs Computer Organization. Explain Von Neumann Architecture vs Harvard Architecture with block diagrams. Explain the Von Neumann Bottleneck.

Explain Computer Performance Metrics: Clock Cycle Time, Clock Rate, CPI (Cycles Per Instruction), MIPS, MFLOPS, and CPU Execution Time formula: $T_{CPU} = \text{Instruction Count} \times \text{CPI} \times T_{clk}$. Explain Amdahl's Law: $\text{Speedup} = \frac{1}{(1-f) + f/s}$.
Compare RISC (Reduced Instruction Set Computer) vs CISC (Complex Instruction Set Computer) architectures on instruction format, addressing modes, register file size, pipelining, and CPI.

Explain Instruction Formats: 3-Address, 2-Address, 1-Address (Accumulator), and 0-Address (Stack-based) instructions. Write assembly code for evaluating $X = (A + B * C) / (D - E * F)$ using 3, 2, 1, and 0-address instructions.

Explain Addressing Modes: Immediate, Direct (Absolute), Indirect, Register, Register Indirect, Displacement (Relative, Base-Register, Indexed), and Auto-increment/decrement with effective address (EA) calculations and use cases.

Explain Booth's Multiplication Algorithm for signed 2's complement binary integers. Multiply multiplicand $M = (-9)_{10} = (10111)_2$ by multiplier $Q = (-5)_{10} = (11011)_2$ using 5-bit Booth's algorithm showing registers $A, Q, Q_{-1}$, and bit count at each step.

Explain Division Algorithms for unsigned binary integers: Restoring Division Algorithm vs Non-Restoring Division Algorithm. Divide dividend $Q = (11)_{10} = (1011)_2$ by divisor $M = (3)_{10} = (0011)_2$ using Non-Restoring Division showing register steps.

Explain IEEE 754 Floating-Point Standard representation: Single Precision (32-bit: 1 sign, 8 exponent with bias 127, 23 mantissa) and Double Precision (64-bit: 1 sign, 11 exponent with bias 1023, 52 mantissa). Represent $(-12.625)_{10}$ in IEEE 754 single precision format.
Explain Carry Look-Ahead (CLA) Adder. Derive carry generate ($G_i = A_i B_i$) and carry propagate ($P_i = A_i \oplus B_i$) equations and show how 4-bit CLA eliminates ripple carry propagation delay.
Explain Instruction Cycle: Fetch, Decode, Execute, Interrupt cycles. Explain Register Transfer Language (RTL), micro-operations (Register transfer, Arithmetic, Logic, Shift), and bus architecture.

Explain Control Unit Design: Hardwired Control Unit (State machine / PLA design) vs Microprogrammed Control Unit (Control Memory, Microinstruction format, Microprogram Sequencer). Compare Hardwired vs Microprogrammed control in speed, flexibility, and cost.
Explain Horizontal Microinstruction vs Vertical Microinstruction formats with examples.

Explain Instruction Pipelining: 5-Stage MIPS Pipeline (IF, ID, EX, MEM, WB) with space-time diagram. Derive theoretical speedup of a $k$-stage pipeline for $n$ instructions: $S_k = \frac{n \cdot k}{k + n - 1}$.

Explain Pipeline Hazards: (1) Structural Hazards (Resource conflicts), (2) Data Hazards (RAW, WAR, WAW dependencies and Forwarding/Bypassing solution), (3) Control/Branch Hazards (Branch prediction: Static vs Dynamic, Branch Target Buffer - BTB, Delayed Branching).
Explain Superscalar Processors, Superpipelining, Very Long Instruction Word (VLIW), and Vector Processing.

Explain Memory Hierarchy: Registers, Cache Memory (L1, L2, L3), Main Memory, Secondary Storage in terms of speed, cost, and capacity. Explain Principle of Locality of Reference (Temporal Locality vs Spatial Locality).

Explain Cache Memory Mapping Techniques with diagrams and tag/index/offset address divisions:
(a) Direct Mapping,
(b) Associative (Fully Associative) Mapping,
(c) Set-Associative Mapping (K-Way Set Associative).
Given a 32-bit physical address, $64\text{ KB}$ cache size, and $64\text{ bytes}$ block size, determine Tag, Set/Index, and Word Offset bits for 4-Way Set Associative mapping.
Explain Cache Write Policies: Write-Through vs Write-Back (Dirty bit) and Write-Allocate vs No-Write-Allocate. Explain Cache Replacement Policies: LRU, FIFO, and Random.
Explain Virtual Memory and Address Translation using Page Table and TLB. Calculate Effective Memory Access Time (EMAT) given Cache and TLB hit rates.

Explain Input-Output Organization and I/O Data Transfer Modes: Programmed I/O (Busy-waiting / Polling), Interrupt-Driven I/O, and Direct Memory Access (DMA). Compare their CPU utilization and data transfer speeds.
Explain DMA Controller (DMAC) architecture (Address register, Word count register, Control register) and DMA transfer modes: Burst Transfer vs Cycle Stealing vs Transparent DMA.
Explain Interrupt Handling: Priority Interrupts, Daisy Chaining Priority scheme, Software Polling, and Vectored Interrupts.
Explain Flynn's Taxonomy of Computer Systems: SISD, SIMD, MISD, and MIMD with block diagrams and examples.

Explain Multiprocessors and Multicomputers: Shared-Memory Architecture (UMA / Symmetric Multiprocessing - SMP, NUMA) vs Distributed-Memory Architecture. Explain Cache Coherence Problem and Snooping protocols (MESI protocol: Modified, Exclusive, Shared, Invalid) vs Directory-Based protocols.
